faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about DeepValues.AI — what it is, who it's for, and how the research works.
faq.a1: DeepValues.AI is an AI-native financial assistant for individual investors. It runs multi-analyst AI research on any US-listed stock — reading every SEC filing, earnings transcript, and 13F holding — and produces a structured briefing with intrinsic value, financial deep-dive, smart-money positioning, and recent filings. Built by LuLu Ventures LLC and aligned only with the individual investor: no advertiser kickbacks, no promoted stocks, no conflicts of interest.
faq.a2: Individual retail investors who want institutional-grade stock research without paying Bloomberg or FactSet prices. Especially useful if you follow a value-investing approach — the product is built around the methods of Buffett, Munger, Greenblatt, and other legends — but it works for anyone doing fundamental analysis on US stocks.
faq.q3: How is DeepValues.AI different from Yahoo Finance, Seeking Alpha, or Robinhood?
faq.a3: Yahoo Finance gives you raw data. Seeking Alpha gives you crowd-sourced opinions. Robinhood is a broker that profits when you trade. DeepValues.AI is none of those — it's research the user pays for (so we work for you, not for advertisers), generated by AI that reads the actual SEC filings end-to-end, with sources cited on every claim. We don't sell your data, don't promote stocks, and don't get paid when you trade.
faq.q4: What does a research briefing include?
faq.a4: A team of AI research agents writes each briefing from SEC filings and market data. Analysts argue the bull case and the bear case; a portfolio manager weighs both and gives a stance (ADVOCATE, WATCH or AVOID) with a plan for what to monitor. Underneath sits the model: every input behind three valuation methods (free cash flow, Buffett's owner earnings and Damodaran's two-stage model), so you can check the work. Each briefing is dated, and a fresh one re-reads the latest filings and prices.
faq.a5: Buffett Lens is a voice-and-text conversational AI grounded in a specific company's public disclosures. Ask it anything — "how did revenue mix change last quarter?" or "what did management say about AI capex on the last call?" — and it answers with citations to the exact filing or transcript section. Voice audio is processed in real time through Microsoft Azure Speech Services and never stored.
faq.a6: No. DeepValues.AI is an AI research and education product, not a registered investment adviser. AI briefings are factual research and analysis; they are not personalized investment recommendations. You are responsible for your own investment decisions. Every output cites its source so you can verify what the AI tells you.
faq.a7Html: Free: 9 credits at signup, enough for 3 fresh briefings, then 0.75 credits a week (about one fresh briefing a month), with an unlimited watchlist and every guru. Plus: $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year, with a 7-day free trial for first-time subscribers and about 6 fresh briefings a month. A fresh briefing costs 3 credits; credit packs top up either plan, and the API is paid per call from the same credits. Current prices are always on the pricing page.
faq.a8: Yes. We don't sell personal data. We don't use your inputs or chats to train any AI model (ours or our vendors'). Voice audio is never stored — it's streamed to Microsoft Azure for real-time transcription only, then discarded. You can export or delete your account in one click. Full details in the Privacy Policy.

bi.promise: Is the US stock market cheap or expensive? Two valuation gauges answer it at a glance, every trading day.
bi.names: On iPhone it is called Buffett Indicator, on Android Bubble Watch: the same app, with the same data.
bi.heroNote: iPhone: Buffett Indicator, a one-time paid download with no ads. Android: Bubble Watch, free with a small banner ad.
bi.gauges.heading: Two gauges, in plain words
bi.gauges.subtitle: Both ask the same question from different sides: how much are investors paying for US stocks compared with what stands behind them?
bi.buffett.title: Buffett Indicator
bi.buffett.formula: Total US stock market value ÷ US GDP
bi.buffett.body: It weighs the price of every listed US company against the size of the whole economy. Warren Buffett once called it “probably the best single measure of where valuations stand at any given moment.” Above 100%, stocks are worth more than everything the country produces in a year.
bi.shiller.title: Shiller PE (CAPE)
bi.shiller.formula: S&P 500 price ÷ average inflation-adjusted earnings of the last 10 years
bi.shiller.body: Averaging ten years of earnings smooths out booms and recessions, so the ratio shows what you pay for a typical decade of profits. It ran famously high before the 1929 crash, the dot-com bubble and 2008.

bi.f2.body: Charts from six months to the full record: 35+ years of the Buffett Indicator and 140+ years of the Shiller PE, with a trend line and ±1σ / ±2σ bands.

bi.f7.body: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Italian, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Brazilian Portuguese, Hindi and Indonesian.
bi.f8.title: DeepValues inside
bi.f8.body: A DeepValues tab opens DeepValues' value-investing research, for when you want to go from the whole market to single companies.
bi.faq.a1: The total market value of all US stocks divided by US gross domestic product (GDP). It shows how richly the stock market is priced against the economy that earns its profits. The app uses the Wilshire 5000 for market value and official US GDP data.
bi.faq.a2: The S&P 500's price divided by its average inflation-adjusted earnings over the previous ten years, a measure popularized by economist Robert Shiller. Its monthly history goes back to the 1880s.
bi.faq.a3: Both readings refresh once every US trading day. With alerts on, you get a notification when fresh data lands, daily or weekly as you choose.
bi.faq.a4: Bubble Watch on Android is free to download and shows a small banner ad. Buffett Indicator on iPhone is a one-time paid download with no ads and no subscription: $9.99 one-time in the US App Store; other countries see their local price.
bi.faq.q5: Which phones does it run on?
bi.faq.a5: iPhone with iOS 17 or later, where the app is called Buffett Indicator, and Android 8.0 or later, where it is called Bubble Watch. Both read the same data.
bi.faq.a6: No. The app shows public market data for information and education only. It is not investment advice, and it is not affiliated with Warren Buffett or Berkshire Hathaway.
